scope: defensive cybersecurity; sources are references or defensive detection data, not exploit-training material

text_sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
text_sources.notes: Prefer catalog metadata and remediation-oriented context; preserve attribution and check current terms.

text_sources.name: CISA Cybersecurity Advisories
text_sources.use: defensive detection, impact, mitigation, and response summaries
text_sources.notes: Curate mitigation and response sections; review third-party content and reuse terms.

text_sources.name: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3
text_sources.use: incident preparation, response, recovery, and risk management

text_sources.name: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 and SP 800-53A Rev. 5
text_sources.format: official XML and plain-text control/assessment downloads
text_sources.use: security controls, assessment, governance, identity, logging, and incident response

text_sources.name: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework
OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
text_sources.format: Markdown from the official source repository
text_sources.use: selected defensive guidance for authentication, access control, validation, logging, headers, and secure storage
text_sources.license: CC BY-SA 4.0; attribution retained; keep derived artifacts private unless share-alike terms are reviewed

text_sources.name: Cybersecurity Question-Answer-Assertion (QAA) Dataset
text_sources.format: JSON, 1,563 QA records; use only the 445 expert-reviewed entries
text_sources.use: defensive advisory task adaptation and held-out QA evaluation
text_sources.license: MIT; preserve upstream notice; source card warns most entries are not expert reviewed

text_sources.name: HolyCyber defensive cybersecurity instruction dataset
text_sources.format: JSONL chat examples; train split only
text_sources.use: auxiliary defensive instruction data from vulnerability management, detection, response, secure configuration, cloud, identity, governance, and cryptography layers
text_sources.license: mixed per row; importer allows only recorded MITRE defensive-use terms, U.S. Government public-domain sources, or OWASP CC BY-SA 4.0; keep training artifacts private pending license review
text_sources.notes: Filter to selected defensive domains and rows with core_share >= 0.30; remove reference appendices and fenced code. Dataset authors disclose it is not reviewed row by row, so use as auxiliary training data and evaluate on separate expert-reviewed QA.

text_sources.name: Cybersecurity Dataset Fenrir v2.1
text_sources.format: JSONL system/user/assistant triples; train split only
text_sources.use: defensive instruction adaptation, cloud and DevSecOps hardening, incident response, secure configuration, and refusal behavior
text_sources.notes: Upstream card reports 99,870 rows and describes defensive alignment. Cleaned for non-empty user/assistant pairs and exact duplicates before use.

text_sources.name: Threat Intelligence Dataset by reloading01
text_sources.use: defensive incident analysis, response, threat hunting, detection operations, threat modeling, and vulnerability prioritization
text_sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; attribution, non-commercial use, share-alike
text_sources.notes: Train split only; only explicitly allowlisted defensive categories; exclude OpenPhish-grounded rows and offensive categories. Do not redistribute the resulting model commercially without rights review.

text_sources.name: Trendyol Cybersecurity Defense Instruction-Tuning Dataset v2.0
text_sources.use: defensive SFT coverage across cloud security, SOC operations, incident response, and governance
text_sources.notes: Train split only; normalized and exact-deduplicated against other added instruction sources.

text_sources.name: Cosmopedia educational text subsets
text_sources.format: streamed synthetic text from auto_math_text, khanacademy, and openstax configurations
text_sources.use: a small general-language sample for lexical and syntax breadth only; not cybersecurity evidence or domain knowledge
text_sources.notes: Capped at 500 samples per subset to prevent general educational text from overwhelming cybersecurity data.

text_sources.name: NVD CVE API and data feeds
text_sources.use: vulnerability description, severity, CWE mapping, and remediation references
text_sources.notes: Avoid treating severity alone as a complete risk score; join with asset context and KEV status.

tabular_defense_sources.name: UNSW ToN_IoT
tabular_defense_sources.use: labeled IoT/IIoT telemetry, OS, and network anomaly detection
tabular_defense_sources.notes: Use for a separate defensive detection model; inspect terms, labels, and provenance first.

tabular_defense_sources.name: CSE-CIC-IDS2018
tabular_defense_sources.notes: Large; download only if needed. The source page requires citation on use or redistribution.

not_a_claim: These sources do not cover 90% of cybersecurity work. Define task coverage and evaluate each task separately.
